results.title: Claude has become exhausting to use, and I'm starting to regret paying for it
results.content:
I was using Claude Code per usual one day. It was a busy day, so I was at 90% of my session limit when Claude suddenly decided it was time to call it quits. Instead of continuing with the task I'd asked it to complete, it essentially told me I was getting too close to my usage limit and that it would be better to stop there. It kept pushing the fact that I'm approaching my limit, and this isn't something I had noticed before.

I assumed it was an one-off quirk initially, and brushed it off. Then I started seeing other Claude users complain about the exact same thing. Over the past few days, I've come across multiple Reddit posts from users reporting that Claude has started slowing down or outright refusing to continue working once they're close to their usage limits. [...] Despite all the good things I've had to say about Claude all these months, one thing I've continuously whined about is its usage limits. They're terrible, and they keep getting worse. However, the usage limits themselves aren't what I'm going to complain about here. Somehow, Claude has found a way to make them even more frustrating by occasionally deciding for me that I'm too close to my limit to keep working. [...] In one particularly ridiculous example, a Claude Max 20x user said Claude Design noticed they were at 90% usage and decided it would be safer not to start the task at all. They eventually got it to cooperate, but only after asking four times. The funniest part is that the task itself ended up consuming less than 1% of their allowance.

Claude refusing to do the task until limit is reset

Another user reported Claude Code repeatedly stopping once their usage reached around 90%, even after they'd added instructions to their CLAUDE.md telling it to ignore usage warnings and keep working. They said the behavior had gotten to the point where they had to babysit Claude, only to discover midway through testing that several things they'd asked it to do hadn't actually been completed.

# What to Do When Claude Hits Its Limit Mid-Session

by Haroon Akram

Imagine you are in the middle of a chat session with Claude when it hits its limit. There is nothing more frustrating than this. There are important things in the chat to carry out and get the task completed on time. But when you have consumed all the credits, there is nothing you can do except to wait for the rollover of the 5-hour window to complete. Here arises a question of what to do when Claude hits its limit mid-session? As the answer is based on human experience, no AI engine can answer this, even if they are so powerful. [...] Start a new conversation: Open a completely new chat with Claude instead of continuing the old one. This sometimes lets you keep working on small tasks right away, even while the old chat is still locked. It only takes a few seconds to try.
 Switch to a lighter model: Claude has different versions. Opus is the most powerful, but it also fills the tank the fastest. Sonnet and Haiku are lighter versions. They fill the tank more slowly. This is the key idea behind the five-hour Claude usage window reset. If you switch to Sonnet or Haiku, you can often keep working right away. Most writing jobs, summaries, and everyday tasks work very well with Sonnet or Haiku.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long duration task
2. Use up all tokens until limit expires
3. After the mandated delay, ask Claude to resume where it was before the usage limit was reached

## Expected Behavior

Claude should continue exactly where it was interrupted without wasting tokens on figuring out what to do next, often missing the context and wasting even more tokens

## Actual Behavior

Claude never resumes the interrupted step. It always goes back to reading the plan and gets it wrong most of the time.
